svg.text: TEACHER ANCHOR: CCSS.7.SP.C.8 • TEKS 111.27.b.6.B • UNSPSC 60101700 • TITLE I / IV GRANT ELIGIBLE • MODEL: SC6
LESSON GUIDE: 2d6 SAMPLE SPACES & INDEPENDENT EVENTS
Step-by-Step Hands-On Tutorial: Why 7 is the Most Likely Roll (P = 6/36)
Grades 5–10 Probability, Statistics & Random Variables • Hands-On Classroom & Home STEM Studio Series

text.tspan: Examine the 6 × 6 grid on the lid stage.
Die 1 rows (1-6) × Die 2 columns (1-6) = 36 total outcomes.
Every individual pair (like [3,4] or [6,1]) has probability 1/36.

g.text: STEP 2: COUNT PATHS TO EACH SUM

text.tspan: Trace diagonals of constant sum across the grid:
3. SAMPLE EXPERIMENTAL RUNS: Roll 2d6 three times: 7, 4, 10.
4. COMPUTE SAMPLE MEAN: Calculate mean on calculator:
Press Dice & Statistics Icon ([🎲], [Σ+] & [g][x̄]) and run [g] [CLΣ] 7 [Σ+] 4 [Σ+] 10 [Σ+] [g] [x̄] → 7.

g.text: CORE PRINCIPLE: THE BIRTH OF THE BELL CURVE

text.tspan: Single dice have flat uniform distributions (each face is 1/6). But when two dice add together,
extreme sums require extreme coordination, while central sums have many different additive combinations!
This combinatorial clustering is the foundation of the normal distribution Bell Curve!

g.text: ★ NOW YOU TRY! (STUDENT PRACTICE CHALLENGE): EVEN SUM PROBABILITY

text.tspan: Count all 2d6 combinations that give an EVEN sum (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12). Exactly 18 out of 36 outcomes! P = 50.0%! (Scan QR for 3D animated solution!)

g.text: → Build with your blocks, then scan the QR code to watch the animated 3D solution on your screen!
